<@808969530608451584> can you share your full kt config with client images? 🙂 was able to recreate the issue with this config fwiw I was running with ` --image-download always` ``` participants_matrix: el: - el_type: geth el_image: ethpandaops/geth:marius-engine-getblobs-v2 cl: - cl_type: lighthouse cl_image: ethpandaops/lighthouse:peerdas-devnet-6 supernode: true - cl_type: lighthouse cl_image: ethpandaops/lighthouse:peerdas-devnet-6 supernode: false network_params: electra_fork_epoch: 0 fulu_fork_epoch: 1 max_blobs_per_block_fulu: 64 target_blobs_per_block_fulu: 48 num_validator_keys_per_node: 256 additional_services: - dora - spamoor spamoor_params: image: ethpandaops/spamoor:blob-v1 spammers: - scenario: blob-combined config: throughput: 10 sidecars: 2 blob_v1_percent: 100 ``` thx, was able to reproduce it 🙂 the problem is that geth doesn't accept V1 blob transactions yet, but spamoor sends all transactions as v1 after fulu activation. so all transactions are rejected as there are only geth pairs. excerpts.author: jtraglia
excerpts.content:
So for deneb/electra, the limit is based on the number of blobs. For example:
```
MAX_REQUEST_BLOB_SIDECARS_ELECTRA = MAX_REQUEST_BLOCKS_DENEB * MAX_BLOBS_PER_BLOCK_ELECTRA
```
This allows a node to request all of the blobs for those blocks it received. With the current `MAX_REQUEST_DATA_COLUMN_SIDECARS` this is no longer the case. If you receive 128 blocks, you'll need to make several data column sidecar requests.
